subject: fat-tailed dwarf lemur
title: This Primate Hibernates for 7 Months and Its Cells Get Younger

scenes.text: One primate sleeps seven months a year, and its cells come out younger.
The fat-tailed dwarf lemur of Madagascar is the only primate known to hibernate.
It lives off fat stored in its tail. Its heart drops from about two hundred beats a minute to under eight.
It takes a breath roughly once every ten minutes.
In 2025, Duke scientists found its telomeres, the aging caps on its chromosomes, grew longer during hibernation.
The catch? Two weeks after waking, they shrank right back.

description:
The fat-tailed dwarf lemur is the only primate known to hibernate, for up to seven months, living on fat stored in its tail; its heart rate falls from about 200 to under 8 beats a minute.
A 2025 Biology Letters study at the Duke Lemur Center found its telomeres lengthened during hibernation, then returned to normal within about two weeks of waking.
Would you hibernate if it made you younger?
first_comment: Dwarf lemurs can live nearly 30 years, about twice as long as similar-sized primates. Would you sleep seven months a year for that?
